test_title: PYST 3: SSC CGL Tier - II (English) (Held on: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: english
question:
**Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Expert designers standardize basic designs, leaving scope for the satisfaction of individual taste.

B. However, uniformity does not imply a lack of taste.

C. Mechanical production of goods leads to uniformity of design.

D. In fact, the popular taste has improved because standardized goods of better design are now accessible.
solution:
The correct answer is 'CBDA.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'C' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "**uniformity of design**". Hence, 'C' is the first part.
 
• Sentence B will come after C as it is giving information about the implication of uniformity.
 
• Sentence D will come after B as it is giving information about the reason behind the enhancement of the taste i.e.** ****standardized goods of better design are now accessible**.
 
• The sentence 'A' is the concluding part as it further explains that **the satisfaction of individual taste develops as expert designers standardize basic designs**.

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *Mechanical production of goods leads to uniformity of design. However, uniformity does not imply a lack of taste. In fact, the popular taste has improved because standardized goods of better design are now accessible. Expert designers standardize basic designs, leaving scope for the satisfaction of individual taste.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **__Hint__**

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.
